open_question_notes:
More contortion on the contact push (left as it is): the twist works within its caps. But the central kick alone already spins the head at 41-47 rad/s in a stagger: with the contact push on, the head peaks at 41.0 rad/s against its 14 rad/s cap, and with the central kick only it peaks at 47.1 (probe1.log, CHAIN). So the joint limits and pose springs, not the twist, decide how much the body contorts, as A reported.

The grab's lens pull-back and the bend's depth (left as they are):
- The hold rise (0.10 m) is larger than the bend's eye drop (0.083 m: rig eye at 1.568 m held, 1.651 m standing). The pull-back (0.24 m, which puts the lens 0.20 m behind EyePoint) is larger than the bend's forward lean (about 0.12 m).
- The eases run on their own timers (0.2 s in, 0.45 s out), while the pose blends finish in about 10 ticks. So the lens rises 4.7-6.4 cm above the standing view and sinks back on every grab and release (finding 3).
- On an LB release the victim stands up 0.5 m in front of the lens. Its cap rises through the middle of the view while the view eases back up (grab_release_moment.png, frames about 134-138). It covers at most 30% of the view, with the nearest point 0.40 m away (probe4), which is within the first-person rules. The LB release is never checked by the lens test (finding 6).

The combat log over the knee contact (I'm to propose a fix, as a spec question):
- What I see: in grab_knee_sheet.png (frames 69-70) the CombatLog panel covers the knee's contact star and the victim's right shoulder. Its node in hud.tscn:78-89 is anchored right-centre, offsets -800..-40 by -40..+204 px. In side view the same panel sits over the struck dummy's torso (pppp_jabs_zoom.png).
- Proposal: move it to the top-right corner (anchor_top 0, offset_top about 110 px so it clears the camera toast, width about 560 px) and show 6 entries. Or keep it where it is but fade it to about 35% opacity while get_hold_view_weight() > 0 and in side view.
- Either way it stays the SPEC §11 overlay (the last hits with timing), so only its placement changes. That is Game-boy's call.

The side-view flash minimum size (left as it is):

findings.title: Contact flash misses the struck body: no flash from a thrown pipe, a faint one from body impacts, and the wrong part on a staggering body
findings.detail:
HumanoidRig.flash_at() (game/actors/humanoid_rig.gd:400-430) puts the overlay at the raw world contact point. It anchors the point to whichever drawn bone follower has the nearest origin. The shader only whitens pixels within hit_flash_radius_m (0.25 m, full strength to 0.125 m) of that point. So any contact point that is not on the body as drawn loses the flash.
(a) Off-body contact points: weapon.gd:118 uses the pipe's origin, which touches the 0.35 m CharacterBody capsule, not the meshes. CombatActor._impact (combat_actor.gd:1307) uses the midpoint between the two bodies at 1 m height. A thrown pipe's point lands 0.293 m from the nearest mesh (falloff 0, no flash). A flying-body knockdown's lands 0.178 m away (at most 61% white, on the edge).
(b) Bodies already ragdolling: HitDetector's contacts sit on hurtboxes, which follow the animation. A staggering body (partial ragdoll at the approved 0.9 influence) or a lying ragdoll is drawn 0.2-0.35 m away from them. In P P P P, the uppercut lands on the hook-staggered dummy's head, but the flash anchors to BoneLeftUpperArm, 0.363 m from the drawn head. The head doesn't flash; the shoulder does.
README's approved departure says the victim flashes white around the point the hit landed. Before the localization all these hits flashed (whole body). Flash plus ragdoll was a known untested pair (HANDOFF 10:55), and test_hit_flash.gd only uses HitDetector contacts on bodies that are not ragdolling.
findings.evidence: captures/review_code/probe7.log: 'PIPE: weapon_throw on Dummy1 (body impact true): flash point 0.293 m from the nearest drawn mesh; falloff there 0.00' and 'IMPACT: impact_body_knockdown on Dummy2: 0.178 m; falloff 0.61'. probe3.log: 'uppercut HEAD state=LAUNCHED ragdoll=FULL nearest=Head drawn-vs-hurtbox 0.233 m; flash anchor BoneLeftUpperArm, flash point 0.363 m from the drawn Head'. probe2.log: 'STAGGER FLASH: ... flash point 0.346 m from the drawn head (radius 0.25)'. Capture pipe.avi frames 176-177 (pipe_throw_zoom.png): no white on the struck dummy except a faint smear on the thigh under the burst. Code: humanoid_rig.gd:413-421, weapon.gd:118, combat_actor.gd:1307.
findings.repro: From the worktree: godot --headless --fixed-fps 60 -s addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd -gdir=res://captures/review_code/ -gprefix=probe_review7 -gexit (and -gprefix=probe_review3). Or play combo_bot 'Pipe: pick up, 3 swings, throw' and step to frames 176-177, or 'P P K' into a second dummy.
findings.suggested_fix:
In HumanoidRig.flash_at, map the point onto the struck part as drawn:
1. Find the hurtbox nearest the point (distance to its capsule segment or sphere minus its radius).
2. Clamp the point onto that hurtbox (closest point on its segment plus the offset, limited to its radius).
3. Express the point in the animation frame of that hurtbox's bone_a (global_transform * _bone_globals[bone]).
4. Place it on, and follow it with, the same bone's drawn follower (_bone_nodes[bone].to_global(local)).
That fixes both the off-body contacts and the ragdoll offset. Optionally also compute on-hurtbox contact points in weapon.gd and CombatActor._impact, which the comic effects would use too. Add tests: a thrown pipe and a body impact reach full strength on the struck body, and a re-hit on a staggering body flashes within the core of the drawn struck bone.

findings.title: A respawning dummy ignores ghost bodies and can blink back in inside a body lying on its post
findings.detail:
TrainingDummy._respawn_spot() (training_dummy.gd:263-267) checks for room against LAYER_WORLD, LAYER_PLAYER_BODY and LAYER_ENEMY_BODY only. Bodies that are lying, KO'd (still blinking), getting up, held or flying are ghosts on LAYER_DOWNED_BODY, so a dummy comes back at its post right inside them. With another dummy knocked down onto its post, it came back 0.00 m from the post with a drawn bone of the lying body 0.08 m from its axis (its radius is 0.35 m). The same goes for an enemy the player holds over the post.
Two dummies that come back in the same tick can also pick the same spot. set_post(fresh) leaves the first one a ghost until the next physics step (training_dummy.gd:132-134), and the physics server hasn't moved it yet.
Unlike _move_under_ragdoll(), the ring spots (0.7 m and 1.4 m out) have no check that the path from the post is clear, so a spot past the near-side curb or a crate can be picked. They also have no floor check. While it waits for room, it builds a new CapsuleShape3D and query every sim tick (training_dummy.gd:257-262).
The only test (test_a_dummy_comes_back_beside_its_post_when_someone_stands_on_it) uses a solid player on the post. The approved behaviour says a dummy whose post is occupied comes back at the nearest free spot.
findings.evidence: captures/review_code/probe1.log: 'RESPAWN: d1 lies with its drawn hips 0.08 m (flat) from d0's post' / 'd0 came back 0.00 m from its post; the nearest drawn bone of the body lying there is 0.08 m from its axis (body radius 0.35)'. Code: training_dummy.gd:263-267 (mask), 274-287 (no path or floor check), 257-262 (allocations), 132-134 (ghost until the next step).
findings.repro: Run probe_review.gd test_probe_respawn_into_lying_body: KO dummy 0. When it is gone, set dummy 1 on dummy 0's post and knock it down (downed_frames raised so it keeps lying). Wait for dummy 0 to come back.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CombatTypes.LAYER_DOWNED_BODY to the query mask. The gone dummy is on no layer, so it doesn't block itself. Check the way from the post to each ring spot against LAYER_WORLD with cast_motion, as _move_under_ragdoll does. Build the shape and query once and reuse them. Add tests with a body lying on the post and one held over it.

findings.title: A dummy blinking in still attracts magnetism and blocks a thrown pipe, though no hit can land on it
findings.detail:
During the blink-in, can_be_hit_by() and can_be_grabbed() are false (as approved). But _find_magnet_target() (player.gd:630) skips only KO'd, flying and downed bodies, so the player's strikes lunge and turn toward a body that can't be hit, then whiff. The magnetism cone in debug draw marks it too.
One physics step after it comes back, the dummy is solid on LAYER_ENEMY_BODY. A thrown pipe's mask includes that layer (weapon.gd:86), so the pipe collides, finds can_be_hit_by false, and still bounces off with linear_velocity *= -0.2 (weapon.gd:133), taking no durability. test_nothing_finds_a_body_that_blinked_off covers only the gone body.
findings.evidence: captures/review_code/probe2.log: 'BLINK-IN: invulnerable true, can_be_hit_by false, can_be_grabbed false, magnet target is it true'. Code: player.gd:630, weapon.gd:86, 103-133.
findings.repro: Call dummy.blink_in(), then player._find_magnet_target(jab) (probe_review2.gd test_probe_magnet_blink_in). Or KO a dummy and jab toward its post in the 0.5 s after it comes back.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip bodies that are blinking in (a CombatActor.is_blinking_in(), or is_invulnerable() if get-ups should be skipped too) in _find_magnet_target. Keep the dummy a ghost until its blink-in ends (in TrainingDummy._physics_process, make it solid only once _blink_in_left == 0), or let a thrown weapon pass through a body that is out of reach. Add both cases to test_ko_blink.gd.

findings.title: dummy_revive_s changed meaning under the same preset key, so older presets now give a 5.5 s comeback
findings.detail: Before phase 3, dummy_revive_s counted from the KO (default 2.5 s). It now counts from the blink-off (default 1.0 s, about 4 s from KO to back). Presets store every value (Tuning.preset_dict), so any preset saved before phase 3 holds dummy_revive_s 2.5. apply_preset() loads it as is, with no warning, giving 1.5 + 1.0 + 2.5 + 0.5 = 5.5 s from KO to back. Missing keys are fine: apply_preset starts from the defaults. The old presets also restore ragdoll_partial_influence 0.6, which is expected for a preset.
findings.evidence: tuning_data.gd dummy_revive_s doc and default (2.5 -> 1.0, 'counted from the blink-off', HANDOFF 12:25). training_dummy.gd:242 counts _gone_frames. tuning.gd:306-345 (apply_preset takes saved keys as is; no format migration).
findings.repro: Save a preset on f43ab9a (or write one with "dummy_revive_s": 2.5), load it at c27afaf, KO a dummy and time it until it is back (about 5.5 s instead of 4).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the tunable (for example dummy_revive_after_blink_s) so old presets report it as an unknown key and take the new default. Or bump PRESET_FORMAT and migrate the old value (old - ko_linger_s - ko_blink_s, clamped at 0) with a last_warnings line. Regenerate tuning/default.json.

findings.title: Two tests would still pass with what they guard broken: per-part spin caps, and the lens rules on an LB release
findings.detail:
test_the_contact_push_stays_within_its_caps_after_many_hits_in_a_row (tests/test_ragdoll.gd:993-1027) asserts only the global safety cap: spin < ragdoll_max_spin * 1.25 = 50 rad/s. A single stagger's central kick already spins the head to 47 rad/s, so this test can't tell whether the per-part twist caps (head 14, trunk 8, limb 14 rad/s) hold after many hits. Only test_a_kick_off_center_twists_the_struck_part_within_its_cap checks a per-part cap, on one head kick.
In test_hold_knees_and_throw_keep_the_lens_clear (tests/test_grab_view.gd:318-320), the check skips every tick where the victim isn't GRABBED and no move runs. An LB release, where the victim stands up and its cap rises through the lowered view, is never checked against the 0.3 m, 25 cm and half-the-view rules. Today it passes them: 30% at most, nearest 0.40 m.
findings.evidence: tests/test_ragdoll.gd:1025. captures/review_code/probe1.log: 'CHAIN: central kick only, top head spin 47.1 rad/s'. tests/test_grab_view.gd:318-320. probe4.log: 'RELEASE VIEW LB release: ... most 30% at tick 28, nearest 0.40 m'.
findings.repro: Read the asserts. Set ragdoll_contact_spin_head, trunk and limb to 40 and run test_ragdoll.gd: the many-hits test still asserts only the 50 rad/s bound.
findings.suggested_fix: In the many-hits test, measure each kick's twist the way the single-kick test does: the step's spin with the contact push on minus the same kick's spin with it off, against the struck part's cap. Or record the per-part twist the ragdoll applied (a test accessor) and assert it is within the cap. In the lens test, also run the check for 45 ticks after an LB release and after the third knee's release.
